```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(HTLR)
```

## Coefficient conventions

`fsel` describes the features in the final fitted model. Initializer metadata
identifies the features whose coefficients are supplied. These sets may differ:
`htlr_init()` can describe a subset of `fsel`, and coefficients for omitted
features start at zero in every class. Initializer features outside `fsel` are
rejected. The intercept is always supplied and retained.

With `p` initialized features and `C` response classes, supply a finite numeric
matrix with `p + 1` rows and `C - 1` columns. Coefficients encode log odds relative
to the first level of `factor(y)`. For a factor response, choose the reference
class explicitly by setting its levels. The reference class has no coefficient
column. Binary responses also accept a numeric vector of length `p + 1`, with
the intercept first and remaining coefficients in final `fsel` order.

If an external multinomial method returns coefficients for all `C` classes,
subtract its reference-class column from each other column, including the
intercept row. For example, if `betas` already has columns in response-level
order, use `sweep(betas[, -1, drop = FALSE], 1, betas[, 1], "-")` and name the
resulting columns `levels(factor(y))[-1]`. Check the external estimator's response
and predictor scales before importing its coefficients.

## Align a named matrix safely

This example uses `stats::glm()` to obtain binary coefficients on the supplied
predictor scale. The short HTLR chains illustrate the API; use suitable chain
lengths and convergence checks for inference.

```{r external-coefficients}
set.seed(42)
X <- cbind(gene_a = rnorm(60), gene_b = rnorm(60), gene_c = rnorm(60))
y <- factor(rep(c("control", "case"), 30), levels = c("control", "case"))
external <- glm(y ~ gene_a + gene_b + gene_c,
                data = data.frame(y, X), family = binomial())
deltas <- matrix(coef(external), ncol = 1,
                 dimnames = list(names(coef(external)), "case"))
rownames(deltas)
colnames(deltas)
```

Direct matrix row names must identify exactly one `Intercept` or `(Intercept)`
row and every final fitted feature. Row order may differ from predictor order;
the intercept may appear anywhere. Column names identify the non-reference
classes and may be reordered too. Each named axis must have unique, nonmissing,
nonempty names that match the data. Feature alignment requires unique, valid
`colnames(X)`.

```{r named-alignment}
X_reordered <- X[, c("gene_c", "gene_a", "gene_b")]
set.seed(43)
fit <- htlr(X_reordered, y, init = deltas, stdx = FALSE,
            iter = 4, warmup = 2, leap = 1, leap.warm = 1)
stopifnot(identical(names(fit$feature$fsel), colnames(X_reordered)))
fit
```

An unnamed matrix axis remains positional: feature rows follow `fsel`, and
class columns follow `levels(factor(y))[-1]`. Unnamed rows with non-default
`fsel` warn because feature identity cannot be checked. Prefer names or explicit
metadata over this compatibility mode.

Prediction matrices retain the original column positions used to train that
fit. Names used for initialization or `fsel` do not enable prediction-time
column reordering.

```{r prediction-order}
probabilities <- predict(fit, X_reordered)
stopifnot(nrow(probabilities) == nrow(X_reordered))
head(probabilities)
```

## Initialize fewer features than the final model

Fit the external estimator on a subset, then use `htlr_init()` to identify its
feature and class coefficients. The first row of its matrix must be the
intercept; subsequent rows correspond to `features` in the supplied order.
Optional `classes` identifies non-reference columns; without class metadata or
column names, class columns remain positional. Matrix dimnames, if present,
must agree with explicit metadata.

```{r subset-initialization}
external_subset <- glm(y ~ gene_b, data = data.frame(y, X), family = binomial())
subset_deltas <- matrix(coef(external_subset), ncol = 1)
init <- htlr_init(subset_deltas, features = "gene_b", classes = "case")
set.seed(44)
fit_subset <- htlr(X_reordered, y, fsel = NULL, init = init, stdx = FALSE,
                   iter = 4, warmup = 2, leap = 1, leap.warm = 1)
stopifnot(length(fit_subset$feature$fsel) == ncol(X_reordered))
fit_subset
```

`gene_a` and `gene_c` start at zero but remain in the fitted model and can change
during sampling. To use original column indices instead, construct
`htlr_init(subset_deltas, features = 3L, classes = "case")` for this reordered
matrix, where `gene_b` is column 3. Indices always refer to the `X` passed to
`htlr()`, before `fsel`; they do not refer to the external estimator's column
positions. When using index metadata, remove coefficient row names or set them
to the corresponding index strings, keeping the intercept name first.

## Screen final features separately

`order_ftest()`, `order_kruskal()`, and `order_plain()` return rankings of the input
columns. They do not generate coefficients or determine a model size. `fsel`
accepts unique positive source-column indices or names, preserving supplied
order; omitted or `NULL` selects all columns. Invalid or repeated selections
error. Standardization may subsequently remove singular columns.

```{r final-screening}
ranked <- order_ftest(X, y)
selected <- head(ranked, 2)
set.seed(45)
fit_screened <- htlr(X, y, fsel = selected, init = "random",
                     iter = 4, warmup = 2, leap = 1, leap.warm = 1)
stopifnot(identical(unname(fit_screened$feature$fsel), selected))
fit_screened
```

`lasso_deltas()` and `bcbcsf_deltas()` generate coefficients for every supplied
input column in its original order. To initialize a subset without screening
the final model, call either helper on that subset and wrap its coefficients
in `htlr_init()` with feature names, or with source indices after removing
coefficient row names. The deprecated `rank_fn` and `k` arguments of
`lasso_deltas()` now warn and return all input rows, with zeros for coefficients
omitted from initialization; they do not choose the final model's feature set.

## Match the predictor scale

With generated initializers (`"lasso"`, `"bcbc"`, or `"random"`), the default
standardization subtracts each selected feature's **median** and divides by its
sample standard deviation. Singular columns are dropped. The fit retains centers
and scales for prediction.

Custom matrices, binary vectors, and `htlr_init()` objects skip standardization,
even when `stdx = TRUE`, and report that it was skipped. The stored
`fit$feature$stdx` is then `FALSE`, with zero centers and unit scales. Supply
coefficients on the scale of the predictors passed to HTLR; `stdx = FALSE`
makes this choice explicit.

For coefficients estimated on standardized predictors, transform the predictors
before fitting HTLR and transform new observations with the same training
statistics. HTLR will not automatically recover the earlier transformation.
For example, this workflow uses median centering consistently:

```{r standardized-coefficients}
centers <- apply(X, 2, median)
scales <- apply(X, 2, sd)
transform_X <- function(new_X) {
  sweep(sweep(new_X, 2, centers, "-"), 2, scales, "/")
}
Z <- transform_X(X)
external_std <- glm(y ~ ., data = data.frame(y, Z), family = binomial())
std_deltas <- matrix(coef(external_std), ncol = 1,
                     dimnames = list(names(coef(external_std)), "case"))
set.seed(46)
fit_std <- htlr(Z, y, init = std_deltas, stdx = FALSE,
                iter = 4, warmup = 2, leap = 1, leap.warm = 1)
predict(fit_std, transform_X(X[1:3, , drop = FALSE]))
```

## Memory limits

External initialization can avoid the cost of computing Lasso initial values,
but the HTLR sampler and stored coefficient draws remain dense. Memory use grows
with observations, final fitted features, response classes, and saved draws.
This API does not establish sparse sampling or support for million-feature data
sets. Screen the final model when appropriate and assess memory requirements
separately from choosing an initializer.
